methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $150M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Distalmotion is a Series G robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $150M+ to date. The valuation universe comprises 10 sector peers—one public (277810.KQ) and nine private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics—though no narrow peer set of three or more companies at the same stage or comparable valuation tier exists.

Only one valuation method proved applicable. The stage-progression approach uses the $150M total raised as a baseline proxy and applies a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical of Series G advancement, yielding $188M. A peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient comparable data: while 10 robotics and manufacturing peers exist in the dataset, none satisfied the minimum threshold of three companies matching on stage, adjacency, or valuation tier.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $159M to $216M, with a median of $188M. This range reflects upside and downside scenarios around the stage-progression result but is constrained by reliance on a single methodology. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage or valuation-comparable peers, making it difficult to benchmark Distalmotion's growth trajectory, unit economics, or market positioning against direct competitors. Additional disclosure of revenue, profitability metrics, or named comparable transactions would strengthen conviction in this range.
